quote:
SPA § 7.2(c) makes receipt of all consents listed on Schedule 4.4 a condition to Buyer's obligation to close. Because Schedule 4.4 is empty, this condition is automatically satisfied, and Buyer could be compelled to close without Vantrell's consent.
- After Closing, if Vantrell asserts that the transfer was an unconsented assignment, it may terminate the Supply Agreement on 30 days' notice (§ 14.2, second sentence).
reason: Issue 2 of the memo meets each element. It quotes Supply Agreement § 14.2: a change in ownership of more than 50% is deemed an assignment requiring Supplier's prior written consent. It notes that the sale of 100% of the stock falls squarely within that provision. It identifies Vantrell's right to terminate on 30 days' notice. It explains that SPA § 4.4 / Schedule 4.4 says 'None', so the § 7.2(c) closing condition does not cover the consent. It also says why this matters to the client (sole-source supply, and only a capped indemnity claim). The recommended fix is to amend Schedule 4.4 so the consent becomes a closing condition.
